1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate letter and line spacing across all screenshots, though not explicitly a specialized dyslexia font.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case with no italics, all-caps, or dense text blocks; all labels and messages are short and clear.

3.why: Content starts readable at mobile width, but repeated error banners stack and increasingly crowd the layout in later screenshots.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Sign in to start your security setup' and the error text are short and in plain language.

5.why: An explicit example 'Example: marcus@example.com' appears under the email field, plus demo credentials are shown in a callout.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long block of text; all copy is brief labels, short sentences, or single-line errors.

7.why: No long codes or secrets (OTP/recovery) ever appear in the flow; only a password field is shown, so copy support for long codes is absent.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is offered on any of the eight screenshots.

9.why: The password field shows 'Use your saved password' and the email is pre-filled, indicating autofill/password-manager support.

10.why: 'Step 1 of 4 · Sign in' is visible at the top and the primary blue 'Sign in' button stands out clearly on every screen.

11.why: Only one main action (Sign in) is presented per screen; no competing primary actions appear.

12.why: Failed attempts only repeat the same error banner without stating success/next steps, and the messages accumulate rather than confirming what happened cleanly.

13.why: Retry is possible but each attempt adds another error banner as a visual penalty; no reveal/hide or re-request controls for codes are present.

14.why: The error 'Check your email and password, then try again' states the problem and fix without blaming the user, though it is generic and stacks.

15.why: No time limits, countdowns, or expiring timers are visible on any screen for reading or entry.
